title: Token flow banding & streaming baseline pilot
creator: Aisha K. Patel
description: Run a controlled pilot to evaluate a banded per-token pricing model that treats token 'flow' (client->model vs model->client) differently for high-stream vs request-response patterns. The goal is to find a simple, customer-understandable baseline that reduces per-token cost regressions for long-output streaming workloads while preserving fairness for input-heavy workloads. This ticket captures experimental design, simulations, rollout gating, enterprise contract mapping, and the security questionnaire implications for hosted API billing changes.
acceptance_criteria: Billing simulation runs across top-200 customers with < 3% median bill delta for standard LLM chat workloads
No more than 5% increase in billing-related support tickets in the first 4 weeks of pilot
Finance approves net revenue projection and unit economics model (sheet linked)
Legal approves contract addenda language for minimums and streaming floors
Security questionnaire mapping updated for new line items and approved by Security
experiment_design: Three cohorts: 1) Control: current flat per-token pricing. 2) Flow-banded: tokens split into IN (user->model) and OUT (model->user) with different per-token bands and a soft monthly floor for streaming flagged sessions. 3) Stream-grace: same as 2) but adds a 30-day grace credit for streaming handshake and small bursts. Assign customers by volume buckets (top 20 enterprise, next 180 mid), run for 4 weeks plus 2-week analysis window. Use server-side flagging to mark streaming sessions (existing telemetry).
metrics: latency: no impact (verify) to token throughput / tail latency
adoption: opt-in rate for streaming-grace after initial announcement
decisions: Use a 2-band approach for OUT tokens: 0-2k tokens and >2k tokens, with reduced per-token for the first band to avoid penalizing short chats
Stream sessions will be identified by websocket handshake + duration > 10s; this is implementation-leveraged telemetry used in other experiments
Apply a soft monthly minimum only to customers in reserved or enterprise tiers for the pilot (to limit churn risk)

risks: Enterprise customers misunderstand floor mechanics and escalate to CSMs
Edge cases in streaming detection misclassify bursty request-response as streaming, causing unexpected bills
Material revenue downside if top customers move to lower tiers in reaction—mitigate with opt-out and clear comms
Security questionnaire updates may increase contract negotiation time for new enterprise deals
rollout_plan: Week 0: Deploy billing flag and simulation hooks in staging
Week 1: Run shadow billing simulation on production traffic (no customer billing changes, only internal reports)
Week 2-5: Enable experiment cohorts for opt-in enterprise customers and select mid-market buckets
Week 6: Freeze and analyze metrics, prepare decision memo
Gate: Proceed to broader rollout only if revenue delta within expected band and support tickets under threshold
testing_plan: Unit tests for token direction attribution and band thresholds
Integration test for billing pipeline split and invoice rendering
Manual validation of 10 sampled streaming sessions for correct classification
Load test to ensure no added latency on token metering path
